title: Secret count_combat_teams (descriptor 26 +0x2B1C) live CS:IP trace attempt
goal: Extend tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1 to arm a runtime CS:IP breakpoint at Secret's candidate_secret_of_the_silver_blades_count_combat_teams function (GAME.OVR+0x3AC6D, VROOMM descriptor 26, relative +0x2B1C -- see tools/map_secret_runtime_symbols.py and docs/engine/research/secret-runtime-symbols.generated.md) during the natural combat-team-counting moment, so the candidate can be promoted only if a genuine execution stop lands exactly there with an exact byte match against the retail body.

code_change.technique: Unlike the resume setter (whose relocated-copy segment was only findable post-hoc), an offline scan of every RAM snapshot from the 2026-07-17 r4 resume-setter proof run (build/dosbox-x-secret-combat-resume-setter-20260717-r4-final/*.ram) found the 84-byte count_teams body resident at a paragraph-aligned physical address (runtime IP == descriptor-relative file offset 0x2B1C, no header/thunk offset) continuously from the very first post-Begin snapshot onward. Segment 362D was resident from selector-hit.ram through post-load-monster.ram; segment 3BCE was resident from combat-gate.ram (a later mtime despite the name) through post-resume.ram -- i.e. VROOMM relocates descriptor 26 to a new physical location partway through the tactical/outcome window. The new code (a) derives the initial destination segment(s) directly from the already-captured operand-parser RAM snapshot (a confirmed-stopped point, same discipline as the pre-existing resume-setter arm immediately above it in the script) and arms BP <segment>:2B1C there before any further RUN, and (b) re-scans every genuine stop's own fresh RAM dump inside the existing outcome-window polling loop and arms any newly-discovered segment on the fly, then checks whether that exact stop's own live CS:IP equals any armed target and byte-verifies the resident 84 bytes against the retail candidate body.
code_change.offline_verification: The Find-CountTeamsSegments search logic (Latin-1 string IndexOf substring search + paragraph-alignment check) was extracted and run standalone in pwsh against the two real copied r4-final RAM files: post-load-monster.ram -> 362D, outcome-stop-001.ram -> 3BCE. Both match the independent Python cross-check performed before implementation. This proves the detection logic is correct; it has not yet been exercised end-to-end inside a live, successfully-completed DOSBox-X run this session (see attempts below).
code_change.secondary_hardening: The pre-existing load-return checkpoint (waiting for CS=32DE EIP=00002DDF after Begin/slot input) used a single fixed Start-Sleep + one-shot BPLIST check, unlike most other checkpoints in the same script which poll with a deadline. Changed to a 30s poll loop (same pattern as the cursor loop and tools/trace_coab_symbol_bytematch.ps1's post-read wait). Backward compatible (strictly more patient), but did not resolve the failures observed this session (see attempt 5).
code_change.followup_fix: Attempt 6 (see live_attempts below) proved the new -ArmCountTeamsBpm logic live-correct (armed BP 362D:2B1C from the operand-parser RAM snapshot, confirmed via BPLIST) but then hit a pre-existing, unrelated bug in the -InjectCombatVictory foe-count sanity poke: it hardcoded 'expected 05' at parserDGroup+0x87CD, but the live foe count naturally varies per combat encounter (attempt 6 observed 8). Fixed by peeking the live byte first and using that actual value as the poke's own expectation (still writing 00 as the replacement, so the bounded-victory intent is unchanged). This is a narrow, directly-blocking pre-existing-mechanism fix, not a change to the count-teams arm/detect logic itself.

Reached load-return, Begin selector, selector-consumer, and operand-parser checkpoints (all confirmed). At operand-parser, Find-CountTeamsSegments correctly derived segment 362D from the live RAM snapshot and armed it: debugger console shows 'DEBUG: Set breakpoint at 362D:2B1C' followed by a BPLIST readback confirming 'BP 362D:2B1C' registered alongside the pre-existing breakpoints -- this is the first live, successful exercise of the new arm/detect code this session. The cursor loop then proceeded through combat-gate.ram and post-load-monster.ram. The run then failed inside the pre-existing -InjectCombatVictory mechanism at tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1 (line ~615, before this attempt's fix): 'RuntimeError: poke expectation failed at 0x26c4d: expected 05, found 08'. 0x26c4d is parserDGroup+0x87CD, the same address this session's new count-teams hit-detection code reads as foes_count -- this run's actual foe count was 8, not the hardcoded 5 the pre-existing script assumed.

This specific failure is therefore very unlikely to be caused by GameLink cross-talk with that particular foreign process, though it does corroborate that the concurrent-multi-agent-DOSBox-X environment described in the coordinator's urgent note remains live and ongoing throughout this session.
live_attempts.note: Root cause identified as a pre-existing script bug, not a code defect in the new arm/detect logic: the -InjectCombatVictory foe-count sanity poke hardcoded an 'expected' value of 05 that is not guaranteed across combat encounters. Fixed by reading the live byte via `python dosbox_gamelink.py peek` first and using that actual value as the poke's own expectation (still overwriting to 00 to force the bounded injected victory) -- see code_change.followup_fix below. This fix is narrowly scoped to the one line that was blocking the requested live test and does not touch the count-teams arm/detect logic itself.

concurrent_environment_evidence.observation: Get-Process -Name dosbox-x showed a dosbox-x.exe process not belonging to this session's own tracked PID at multiple points spanning the whole task: PID 25148 (before attempt 1), PID 58240 (StartTime 15:53:38, after attempt 2), PID 57608 (StartTime 15:55:14, ~96s later), PID 21668 (StartTime 15:58:09, present through and after attempt 5). This is consistent with the mid-task coordinator note that multiple agents were running DOSBox-X concurrently in this shared environment during this exact window.
concurrent_environment_evidence.gamelink_namespacing_gap: tools/dosbox_gamelink.py:15-16 defines fixed, non-namespaced Windows shared-memory object names (MAPPING_NAME = 'DWD_GAMELINK_MMAP_R4', MUTEX_NAME = 'DWD_GAMELINK_MUTEX_R4') with no per-process or per-session scoping. Two concurrently-running DOSBox-X + GameLink instances would contend for or silently share the same named mapping. This is consistent with, though not proven in isolation to be the sole cause of, the observed failure modes (a GameLink input timeout in attempt 3; input calls succeeding but the target instance's own boot/menu state never advancing as expected in attempts 1/2/4/5).

conclusion.reason: Two compounding blockers, both environmental/availability, not logic defects. (1) Attempts 1-5 never reached the operand-parser checkpoint where -ArmCountTeamsBpm first executes, consistent with concurrent multi-agent DOSBox-X/GameLink contention. (2) Attempt 6 broke through that -- it reached operand-parser, correctly derived segment 362D from live RAM, and armed BP 362D:2B1C with a BPLIST-confirmed live registration (the first genuine exercise of the new code this session) -- but then hit a separate, pre-existing, unrelated bug (hardcoded foe-count expectation) before reaching the outcome-window hit-detection loop. That bug is now fixed. Attempt 7, which would have been the first attempt with a fully working harness end-to-end, could not be launched at all: a foreign agent's DOSBox-X session (PID 55564) occupied the machine continuously through a bounded ~9-minute synchronous wait, and per the project's concurrency-safety protocol a second GameLink session must not run alongside it. This is NOT a negative result about whether count_teams gets hit during natural combat-team-counting -- that question remains genuinely untested end-to-end live; the closest evidence is the offline-verified detection logic (Find-CountTeamsSegments correctly locates 362D/3BCE from real captured RAM) plus attempt 6's live confirmation that the arm step itself works.
conclusion.claim_boundary: docs/engine/BUILD-QUEUE.md's 'Capture a Secret runtime CS:IP hit at descriptor 26 +0x2B1C' checkbox stays unchecked. The candidate_secret_of_the_silver_blades_count_combat_teams symbol stays a candidate (semantic_status: candidate_pending_secret_cs_ip_hit) -- unchanged. No promotion without a live, byte-verified hit; none was obtained.

next_steps: Retry `tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1 -TraceCursor -TraceCombat -InjectCombatVictory -ArmConsumedWordBpm -ArmCountTeamsBpm` once `Get-Process -Name dosbox-x` shows zero results (confirmed no other agent has a live DOSBox-X session) before launching. The harness itself (arm/detect logic + the foe-count fix) is now believed ready end-to-end; the remaining blocker the last several attempts hit is purely machine availability, not code.

If concurrent multi-agent DOSBox-X automation continues to be common, namespace tools/dosbox_gamelink.py's MAPPING_NAME/MUTEX_NAME per-PID or per-session (e.g. suffix with the DOSBox-X process id) so concurrent GameLink sessions cannot collide, and/or coordinate a shared lock/queue across agents so no one has to guess-and-wait. Out of scope for this task (shared infra other agents' scripts also call), flagged here for a future round.

The arm/detect logic itself does not need further changes before the next attempt -- it is ready and offline-verified against real captured RAM (segments 362D and 3BCE, matching the independent cross-check), and was additionally live-confirmed to arm correctly in attempt 6.
